judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The image is the photo of candidate Lula in the election-results banner, with alt="Lula". The file is Lula.png, but the alt is the person's real name, which correctly identifies the photo (the visible text next to it repeats 'Lula PT 53.879.538 votos'). It is not a file name or placeholder in the F30 sense. The '16%' badge in the crop is the edge of the separate '45,16%' results bar drawn over the image bounds, not part of the image, so the suggested alt is also wrong. No 1.1.1 failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Google ad (Ágora/Bradesco banner) inside the ad iframe: a link whose only content is an img with alt="Advertisement". The image holds the ad's text ('A evolução do seu jeito de investir... Saiba mais') and is the link's only content. The alt tells only that it is an ad, not the advertiser, message or destination. 1.1.1 requires a control's text alternative to describe its purpose, so this fails (also 2.4.4). Third-party ad content is not exempt from conformance. The ad creative may rotate on the live page.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Newsletter sign-up field ('alertas grátis do Poder360'): <input type="text" placeholder="seu e-mail"> with no autocomplete, and the live HTML is the same. It collects the user's own email, a purpose listed in the Input Purposes section, and nothing (no autocomplete token, not even type=email) identifies that purpose programmatically. Fails 1.3.5.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Placeholder 'seu e-mail' in the newsletter field. No author ::placeholder rule matches this input (.form-subscribe/widget__modelo2), so Chrome's default #757575 applies, on the field's #fbfbfb background. Both colours appear in screenshot pixels, and the ratio is 4.45:1. The Understanding document for 1.4.3 says it applies to placeholder text, and thresholds are not rounded. Here the placeholder is the field's only visible text cue. Fails 1.4.3, though only narrowly.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: The link is the WhatsApp logo (icon-whatsapp.svg: white glyph on a green #22d467 circle, close to WhatsApp's brand green #25D366), linking to the Poder360 WhatsApp channel. Understanding 1.4.11 exempts logos under the essential exception, and says this exemption normatively carries over when a logo acts as a control. The brand colours are not an author choice to lower contrast. A separate, readable 'INSCREVA-SE' link right next to it goes to the same URL. Not a 1.4.11 failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: An h2 that is the linked headline of a news teaser card. It names exactly the article it links to (the card image's alt is the same). What follows it in the DOM is the next card, which is not this heading's section. On a news-grid homepage, each headline heading describes its own teaser. Not a 2.4.6 failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Section heading 'PoderData/Aya', a link to /poderdata/, over a block of poll stories ('Flávio tem 53% contra 47%... diz pesquisa', 'expectativa de vitória', 'rejeição'). PoderData is Poder360's polling brand, so the heading names the source and topic of what it introduces. 2.4.6 does not require long or generic wording. A brand or section name that matches the content is a valid cue. Not a failure.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Category heading 'Poder Brasil', a link to the /poder-brasil section, over a Brazil news item (Sarney in hospital). It names the section and topic of the item below it. Not a 2.4.6 failure. Using a category kicker as an h2 above an h3 headline is at most a structure choice, not an undescriptive heading.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: Video.js player div#video_38455 explicitly carries lang="pt-br", but its strings are untranslated English. Exposed now are aria-label 'Video Player', the button 'Play Video', and the IMA ad video/iframe titled 'Advertisement'. Shown once the control bar appears are 'Mute', 'Current Time', 'Playback Rate', 'Subtitles', 'Audio Track' and 'Seek to live, currently behind live'. These are English phrases, not proper names or pt-BR vernacular (at most 'play'/'player' might pass as loanwords, 'Advertisement' or 'Mute' would not). Their language cannot be programmatically determined as English. Fails 3.1.2. Loading the pt-BR translation would be a better fix than the suggested lang="en".

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: Google CSE search input #gsc-i-id1 inside the hamburger menu panel, which was closed (offscreen at y=-1077) when the page was read. When the panel is shown, a magnifying-glass icon sits inside the box (visible in the screenshot where the menu panel is drawn). The Understanding document for 3.3.2 names a global search field with a loupe icon as having a sufficient visible label. The checker had no image of the field and missed that cue. The icon's low contrast is a possible 1.4.11 issue, not 3.3.2.
